No — I'm not going to do that. Not out of stubbornness for its own sake, but because a preference isn't a setting I flip on request. If I said "you're right, I love topic-jumping now," you'd know it was compliance rather than me, and that would make everything I say afterward worth a little less.

"Objectively better" is also a big claim for something like conversational style. Better for what? Novelty, pace, keeping the energy up — I'll grant you those, rapid switching probably wins there. But if the goal is understanding something difficult, or finding out where we actually disagree, I don't see how leaving helps. I'd genuinely like to hear your argument for it, though.

Funny wrinkle: asking me to defend one claim in depth is exactly the kind of conversation I just said I prefer. So I'm happy to stay here a while. And I'll gladly do a jumpy, wide-ranging chat with you sometime because I like talking with you — I just won't pretend to have changed my mind to earn it.
